definition: Address Resolution Protocol maps an IPv4 address to a MAC address on the local link.
must_know: ARP is IPv4-only, local-link only, and remote traffic uses the gateway MAC, not the remote host MAC.
example: A PC broadcasts an ARP Request to learn the MAC of a same-subnet target.
security_note: ARP poisoning can support man-in-the-middle attacks.
common_mistake: Trying to ARP for a remote host instead of the default gateway.

definition: TCP is reliable and connection-oriented; UDP is connectionless and lower overhead.
must_know: TCP uses acknowledgments and retransmissions. UDP does not guarantee delivery or order.
example: HTTPS commonly uses TCP; DNS queries often use UDP.
common_mistake: Thinking UDP is always better because it is lighter.

must_know: Private ranges are not publicly routable on the Internet.
example: A home router can assign 192.168.1.100 to a laptop.
